message.content:
Below is a quick “recipe” you can copy‑paste into a terminal (or adapt to your favourite language) to post the comment you supplied to VirusTotal.

> **⚠️  Keep your API key secret!**  
> Never commit it to version control or share it publicly.

---

## 1. Using `curl`

```bash
curl -X POST \
     -H "Accept: application/json" \
     -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
     -H "x-apikey: ABC321" \
     -d '{"type":"comment","attributes":{"text":"Confirmed #malware"}}' \
     "https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/ip_addresses/192.168.1.1/comments"
```

### What this does

| Part | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `-X POST` | HTTP method |
| `-H "x-apikey: ABC321"` | Your VirusTotal API key |
| `-H "Content-Type: application/json"` | Tells the server you’re sending JSON |
| `-d ...` | The JSON payload you supplied |
| URL | The endpoint for adding a comment to the IP address 192.168.1.1 |

If everything goes well you’ll get a `201 Created` response with a JSON body that contains the newly created comment’s ID and other metadata.

---

## 2. Using Python (`requests`)

```python
import requests

API_KEY = "ABC321"
IP_ADDRESS = "192.168.1.1"
URL = f"https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/ip_addresses/{IP_ADDRESS}/comments"

payload = {
    "type": "comment",
    "attributes": {
        "text": "Confirmed #malware"
    }
}

headers = {
    "x-apikey": API_KEY,
    "Accept": "application/json",
    "Content-Type": "application/json"
}

response = requests.post(URL, json=payload, headers=headers)

print("Status:", response.status_code)
print("Response:", response.json())
```

---

## 3. Quick sanity check

After posting, you can verify the comment was added by listing all comments for that IP:

```bash
curl -H "x-apikey: ABC321" \
     "https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/ip_addresses/192.168.1.1/comments"
```

You should see your comment in the returned list.

---

### Common pitfalls

| Issue | Fix |
|-------|-----|
| **401 Unauthorized** | Double‑check the API key and that you’re using the correct header (`x-apikey`). |
| **400 Bad Request** | Ensure the JSON payload matches the schema. The example above is the minimal valid payload. |
| **Rate limiting** | VirusTotal may throttle you if you hit the limit. Wait a few seconds and retry. |

That’s it! Once you run one of the snippets, the comment “Confirmed #malware” will be attached to the IP 192.168.1.1 in your VirusTotal account.
